problem: Training ObjectNav agents on the full Habitat 2020 / Matterport3D dataset needs massive compute (e.g. DD-PPO uses 64 GPUs), and map-based methods lengthen paths. Learned policies also do not explicitly exploit the object-room correlation.
motivation: Humans find objects by first finding the likely room and then the object inside it. A reduced dataset lets researchers prototype map-free RL policies on one GPU in hours. Attention over the full memory avoids the recency bias of LSTMs.
key_idea: Condition the goal embedding on scene-classifier features of the current RGB frame to form a joint room-goal representation, and feed it to a Scene Memory Transformer policy trained with PPO.
insight: Adding the scene-classification/goal joint representation to SMT gives large gains on seen scenes: SPL 0.345 to 0.649, SR 0.595 to 0.883, DTS 1.562 to 0.403 (SMTSC vs SMT w/o SC). SMT-based policies also clearly beat the LSTM (SR 0.247), which is consistent with attention over the whole memory helping. Generalization to unseen scenes stays poor (SR 0.08), since only 6 training scenes are used.
method: Small MP3D dataset: 6 of 56 MP3D training scenes, 5 goal classes (chair, cushion, table, cabinet, sink), 3000 train episodes, 600 seen val/test each, plus unseen val/test sets from 2 other scenes (100 episodes each)
Feature encoders: frozen Taskonomy semantic-segmentation features (256-d) and scene-classification features (128-d); goal, relative pose (x,y,sinθ,cosθ) and previous action are each encoded to 32-d
Scene-goal joint representation δ: FC over the concatenation of scene-class features and the goal embedding, giving a goal representation conditioned on the current room
Fused observation embedding φ(o): FC over [seg features, pose, previous action, δ], producing a 256-d vector

Scene Memory Transformer policy: memory of all past φ(o); 8-head self-attention encoder over memory, 8-head attention decoder with φ(o) as query, then FC and softmax to a categorical action distribution
Training: PPO, batch size 64, Adam with LR 1e-5, single V100, in Habitat

setting.backbone: Scene Memory Transformer policy (trained from scratch with PPO) on frozen Taskonomy features
setting.training_data: Small MP3D: 3000 episodes over 6 MP3D scenes, 5 object classes
setting.observation: monocular RGB 640x480 + odometry (x, y, heading relative to start) + previous action + goal category
setting.action_space: low-level: forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 30°, stop
setting.privileged: none (success requires stopping within 0.1 m of the goal object; 500 step limit)

numbers_note: Success rates are printed as fractions (0.883, 0.080) and converted to percent; SPL and DTS are kept as printed. The benchmark is the authors' own reduced dataset, not the official Habitat ObjectNav benchmark. The paper reports no seen/unseen val results.
results: On the seen test set SMTSC reaches SPL 0.649, SR 88.3% and DTS 0.403, well above SMT without scene classification (0.345 / 59.5%) and the LSTM baseline (0.131 / 24.7%). On unseen scenes all methods are weak; SMTSC gets SR 8% vs 4% for the LSTM, Reactive and SMT w/o SC baselines.
limitations: Trained on only 6 scenes and 5 classes, so generalization to unseen scenes is very poor (SR 8%)
Evaluated only on the authors' small custom dataset, with no comparison on the full Habitat ObjectNav challenge and no strong map-based baselines
The unseen set has only 100 episodes, and baselines are reimplementations
